_schema.note: Rate cards, NOT perception cards. There is no 'what people think' side here — both panels are measured facts. Kept in a separate file from perception-items.json because that file's contract is 'a measured perception paired with a measured reality', which these are not.
_schema.critical: These numbers are per 100,000 PEOPLE PER YEAR, not percentages. The perception cards light N of 100 villagers because those numbers are percentages; doing that here would read as 13% when the truth is 13 per 100,000 — wrong by a factor of a thousand. So rate cards draw the lit figures as a COUNT with no 100-slot frame, and the caption always carries the denominator.
_schema.pairing_rule: Both sides of a card must come from the SAME series with the SAME rate_type. The file mixes crude age-specific rates with age-adjusted all-ages rates, and comparing across them is invalid — that trap makes 1932 (17.4 crude) look worse than 2023 (14.2 age-adjusted).

fields.unit: the denominator, printed on the card
fields.rate_type: crude | age-adjusted — must match on both sides
fields.verified: read off the CSV this session

_schema.race_note: Race breakdowns are NOT in the source CSV, which carries only sex and age. They come from CDC directly: Data Brief 464 for rates by race WITHIN sex (2021, the most recent year CDC publishes that cross-tab) and MMWR 74/35 for race overall (2023). Do not mix the two years on one card. CDC states AI/AN suicide deaths are undercounted by roughly 34% through race misclassification on death certificates — any AI/AN figure is a floor.

items.point: Black students attempt suicide at a significantly HIGHER rate. Black men die at half the rate. More people trying and fewer dying is not a fact about despair — it is a fact about method. Firearms are 5% of attempts and 50% of deaths.

items.note: The two rows CANNOT share an axis: attempts are a percentage of high school students, deaths are per 100,000 adult men. Different denominators and different populations. That is why this is two labelled rows and not one chart.

items.ask: In Maine, how are you more likely to die?
items.point: Twenty-one to one. Maine has the lowest homicide rate in America — and it barely registers next to its suicide rate.

items.ask: Washington DC is the only place in America where this is true
items.point: In all fifty states more people kill themselves than are killed. DC is the sole exception — and it also has the LOWEST suicide rate in the country.
